Second problem if any — smaller ritual. Last five complexity and your questions. Stuck line. Two options I…

item.title: Coding Prep 13: Tree DFS
item.description: Tree DFS day. Complements week one BFS level order. Max depth, invert binary tree, same tree. No AI. Speak before solve. Pair with Trees and Graphs in the app. Problem one. Maximum depth of binary tree. Root to leaf longest path length in nodes. Cold open. Six counts. One line recurrence. One through six. Model: if null depth zero. Else one plus max of depth left and depth right. Recursive DFS. Iterative stack or level BFS also works — BFS depth is number of levels. Walk.…

You define dp meaning in one sentence, base cases, recurrence, then iterate bottom up or memo top down. Always state that sen…

item.title: Coding Prep 11: Binary Search + Rotated
item.description: Binary search day. Sorted array lookup, then the rotated array half-sorted trick. Log n comfort for screens. No AI. Speak before solve. Pair with DP Search List binary search questions in the app. Problem one. Classic. Sorted array ascending, find target index or negative one. No duplicates for the base version — clarify. Cold open. Eight counts. Loop invariant and how left right move. One through eight. Model: left zero, right n minus one, while left less or equal right.…

item.title: Coding Prep 10: Linked List Reverse + Cycle
item.description: Linked list day. Reverse a list, then cycle detection with fast and slow. Pointer discipline under stress. No AI. Speak before solve. Pair with DP Search List unit — list section — in the app. Problem one. Reverse a singly linked list. Return new head. Cold open. Eight counts. Iterative three pointers. One through eight. Model: prev null, curr head. While curr: save next, curr next equals prev, prev equals curr, curr equals saved next. Return prev. Draw one two three on pa…

item.title: Coding Prep 9: Merge Intervals
item.description: Merge Intervals. Sort plus linear scan. Shows up in calendars, bookings, and range logic. No AI. Speak before solve. Pair with Intervals and Design in the app. Problem. Given a list of intervals, each a start and end, merge all overlapping ones. Return the merged list sorted by start. Cold open. Ten counts. First step and merge rule. One through ten. Model: sort by start ascending. Keep a current interval. For each next: if next start is less or equal current end, merge —…

item.description: Week two opens with stack muscle. Valid Parentheses, then a quick Min Stack design note. No AI. You speak before I solve. Pair with Stack and Queue in the app. Problem. Model: stack. On open, push. On close, stack must be non empty and top must match this closer — then pop. End: s…

They want clarify, naive, optimize, working code, edges, complexity. Background chat may eat a few minutes. Medium should feel comfortable in thirty to forty minutes with pra…

item.title: Coding Prep 6: Islands + Level Order
item.description: Graphs and trees day. Number of Islands, then Binary Tree Level Order. BFS and DFS flood muscle. No AI. Speak before solve. Pair with Trees and Graphs in the app. Problem one. Grid of water zero and land one. Island is four-connected land. Count islands. Diagonal usually does not connect — clarify. Cold open, eight counts. Approach and complexity. One through eight. Model: scan every cell. When you find land, increment count, then flood fill mark all connected land as wate…

item.title: Coding Prep 5: LRU Cache Design
item.description: LRU Cache. Design problem. Airwallex and many screens love this because it is structure plus clear operations, not a one-shot formula. No AI. You speak the design before code. Pair with the LRU deep drill in the app. Problem. Implement LRUCache with capacity. Methods: get key returns value or negative one if missing. Put key value inserts or updates. When over capacity, evict the least recently used key. Both get and put must be average O of one. Cold open. Ten counts. Name…

item.title: Coding Prep 4: Two Pointers
item.description: Two pointers day. Container With Most Water, then Three Sum moves. Same family: sorted or end-based indices that remove nested loops. No AI. Speak before solve. Pair with Two Pointers unit in the app. Problem one. You have an array height of non-negative integers. Vertical lines at each index. Choose two lines so the container holds max water. Area is min of the two heights times distance between indices. Cold open, eight counts. Naive and optimal move rule. One. Two. Three…

item.title: Coding Prep 3: Longest Unique Substring
item.description: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters. Sliding window muscle. Airwallex medium comfort. No AI. You speak before I solve. After this, open the Longest Substring deep drill in the app. Problem. Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring with all unique characters. Substring means contiguous. Cold open. I'll count to ten. Say: clarifier, naive idea and Big-O, window idea in one sentence. One. Two. Three. Four. Five. Six. Seven. Eight. Nine. Ten. Mod…

item.title: Coding Prep 2: HashMap Family
item.description: Today is the HashMap family. Three shapes, one muscle: memory of what you have already seen. Contains Duplicate. Group Anagrams. Top K Frequent. No AI. You speak before I solve. Airwallex wants process. Naive first. Then the structure. Map or set is not magic — it is O of one average lookup that buys you a linear scan. Cold open. Problem one: given an integer array, return true if any value appears at least twice, else false. I'll count to eight. Out loud: clarifier, naive…

item.title: Coding Prep 1: Two Sum Think-Aloud
item.description: Alright. Interviewer just said: Two Sum. Given an array of integers called nums, and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. I'm going to work this the way I would in a real screen. No AI. Out loud. Naive first, then better. And I'm going to make the mistakes people actually make, so you hear the recovery. Important: you speak before I solve. After this episode, open the tutor app and run the Two Sum deep drill — eight multiple-choice…

Airwallex's engineering blog is unusually clear. The tech screen is like LeetCode easy and medium. They care that you understand basic algorithms and can apply…

item.title: Mock Interview: Financial AI Assistant / AgentOS
item.description: LLM as untrusted planner, never the authorization layer. Tiered action model (Tier 0-3), deterministic policy engine, tool allowlists, server-generated payment intents with canonical summaries, prompt injection defense (6 layers), RAG for documentation, permissioned APIs for account data, step-up authentication for money movement, cross-tenant isolation at infrastructure level.

item.title: Mock Interview: Webhook & Event Delivery Platform
item.description: Transactional outbox pattern for guaranteed event creation, at-least-once delivery with merchant deduplication, per-endpoint queues for tenant isolation, HMAC-signed payloads with timestamp, SSRF protection (DNS rebinding, private IP blocks, redirect limits), exponential backoff with jitter, event replay, and event-list API for recovery.

item.title: Mock Interview: Bulk Payouts & Batch Payments
item.description: Million-row batch processing with streaming validation, deterministic item keys for idempotency, partner-sharded work queues with rate limits, lease-based worker claims, aggregate funding reservation, partial cancellation semantics, and downloadable results. All-or-nothing for validation/funding, independent per-item execution.

item.title: Mock Interview: Bank & Partner Reconciliation
item.description: Reconciliation as a continuous control system, not a nightly report. Immutable evidence ingestion, multi-phase matching algorithm (exact reference then fuzzy candidates), aggregate balance control, exception case management, safe repairs via compensating journals. Zero tolerance for unexplained money differences.

item.title: Mock Interview: Card Authorization & Issuing Platform
item.description: Authorization hold lifecycle, atomic check-and-reserve, deduplication by network transaction ID, clearing matching, partial clearing and incremental authorizations, disputes, stand-in mode with bounded offline limits, and card controls. 150ms SLA for real-time authorization decisions.

item.title: Mock Interview: Multi-Currency Wallet & Double-Entry Ledger
item.description: Immutable double-entry journal as source of truth, balance projections for reads, atomic reserve/settle/release flows, optimistic concurrency with version checks, FX conversion with balanced legs per currency, rounding entries, and balance rebuild from journal replay. Covers the same fundamentals as Airwallex's core ledger system.

item.title: Mock Interview: KYC/Onboarding System
item.description: Multi-jurisdiction KYC, fuzzy name matching (double metaphone + Levenshtein), risk scoring, ongoing monitoring, GDPR pseudonymization, KYC GenAI for false positive reduction, 5-min auto-approval.

item.title: Mock Interview: Idempotent API for Financial Operations
item.description: Client-generated idempotency keys, Redis for speed + PostgreSQL for truth, same-transaction atomicity, unique constraint dedup, saga step idempotency, background reaper for stale records.

item.title: Mock Interview: Low-Latency FX Pricing System
item.description: WebSocket price streaming, sub-100ms end-to-end, best bid/ask aggregation across providers, backpressure throttling, indicative vs tradeable rates, rate audit trail for regulators.

item.title: Mock Interview: Multi-Region Global Infrastructure
item.description: Active-active reads, leader-per-entity writes, synchronous replication, RPO <1min, RTO <5min, data sovereignty per jurisdiction, split-brain prevention, chaos engineering drills.

item.title: System Design Q&A — Power Answers
item.description: Deep Q&A covering the 12 Airwallex interview topics — 5 generic plus 7 domain-specific. For each: killer questions interviewers ask, structured answers that score, common mistakes that lose points, and cross-cutting patterns like RESHADED.

item.title: Back-of-Envelope Estimation Masterclass
item.description: Every number you need for system design interviews, organized around 12 real interview problems. Power numbers, latency defaults, throughput benchmarks, fintech-specific numbers, and how to derive any number from first principles when you forget.

item.title: Mock Interview: Fraud Detection System
item.description: Design a fraud detection system with rule-based + ML ensemble scoring, real-time feature engineering (velocity, amount, location, behavioral), point-in-time correctness, and feedback loops for model improvement. Covers Airwallex's approach to global transaction monitoring with low false-positive rates.

item.title: Mock Interview: Feature Store / ML Infrastructure
item.description: Design a feature store like Airwallex's AirSkiff: batch/streaming unification where the same feature logic works for both real-time and batch, point-in-time joins to prevent ML data leakage, low-latency online serving (2-150ms), and a feature registry for cross-team reuse. 100+ features, 10K TPS serving.

item.title: Mock Interview: Global Treasury Network
item.description: Design a global treasury network for multi-entity cash management: notional pooling, zero-balancing sweeps, payment netting to reduce FX costs, inter-company settlements, and per-jurisdiction regulatory constraints. Covers the same challenges Airwallex faces connecting 50+ countries with capital controls.

item.title: Mock Interview: Metrics & Monitoring Pipeline
item.description: Designing time-series storage, cardinality control, and SLO-driven alerting. Generic system design mock interview.

item.title: Mock Interview: Distributed Job Scheduler
item.description: Designing reliable job scheduling with idempotency, retry, and failure handling. Generic system design mock interview.

item.title: Mock Interview: Security Automation Platform
item.description: Design a security automation platform like the CVE lifecycle system: overnight AI diagnosis, morning dashboard with triaged findings, built-in discussion bot, one-click remediation. Covers SAST/DAST/SCA integration, transitive dependency scanning, and shadow-mode validation — matching Airwallex's security-first fintech requirements.

item.title: Mock Interview: AI Agent Platform (AgentOS)
item.description: Design Airwallex's AgentOS platform: plugin-based AI agents with sandboxed execution, natural-language intent parsing, real-time policy enforcement, and audit trails. Covers the SDD (Spec-Driven Development) pipeline where agents produce specs, users approve, and code is verified against the spec.

item.title: Mock Interview: Distributed Wallet (Auticuro)
item.description: Design a distributed wallet using Airwallex's Auticuro architecture: single-threaded state machine with NO LOCKS, Raft consensus for strong consistency, RocksDB WriteBatch for atomic persistence, client-provided dedup_id for exactly-once semantics. P99 < 20ms at 10K TPS. CQRS with 4-thread design per node.

item.title: Mock Interview: Ride Sharing (Uber)
item.description: Designing driver matching, surge pricing, and real-time location tracking. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

item.title: Mock Interview: Video Streaming (YouTube)
item.description: Designing video upload, transcoding, CDN delivery, and adaptive bitrate. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

item.title: Mock Interview: Rate Limiter
item.description: Designing API rate limiting with token bucket and distributed counters. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

item.title: Mock Interview: Distributed Key-Value Store
item.description: Designing a DynamoDB-like KV store with consistent hashing and quorum. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

item.title: Mock Interview: Web Crawler
item.description: Designing a scalable distributed web crawler with politeness and dedup. Two-voice mock interview with e2e walkthrough and thinking beats.

item.description: YouTube-extracted expert system design interview: designing a payment system like Stripe. Real interview walkthrough with an experienced engineer.

item.title: Mock Interview: Location-Based Service
item.description: Full mock system design interview: designing nearby-driver search and real-time location tracking using geohash, quadtree, and S2 geometry. Two-voice dialogue.

item.title: Mock Interview: Real-Time Chat
item.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a WhatsApp-like messaging system with WebSocket delivery, read receipts, and group chat fan-out. Two-voice dialogue.

item.title: Mock Interview: Top-K / Heavy Hitters
item.description: Full mock system design interview: finding the most frequent items in a data stream at scale using Count-Min Sketch, heaps, and sliding window algorithms. Two-voice dialogue.

item.title: Mock Interview: FX & Multi-Currency Ledger
item.description: Design an FX rate engine with provider aggregation, rate locking with TTL, and a per-currency double-entry ledger with three-entry cross-currency transfers. Covers the same fundamentals as Airwallex's real-time FX engine serving 130+ currency pairs.

item.title: Mock Interview: Object Storage (S3)
item.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a durable object storage system with erasure coding, multipart upload, and 11-nines durability. Two-voice dialogue.

item.title: Mock Interview: Typeahead / Search Autocomplete
item.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a sub-50ms autocomplete system using tries, pre-computed suggestions, and Lambda architecture for freshness. Two-voice dialogue.

item.title: Mock Interview: Notification System
item.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a multi-channel notification system supporting push, email, and SMS with templates, preferences, and delivery tracking. Two-voice dialogue.

item.title: Mock Interview: Distributed Cache
item.description: Full mock system design interview: designing a Redis-like distributed caching system with consistent hashing, virtual nodes, replication, and rebalancing. Two-voice dialogue.

item.title: Mock Interview: Cross-Border Payments
item.description: Design a cross-border payment pipeline with FX conversion, idempotency keys, compliance screening, and bank connector adapters. Covers the full saga pattern with compensating actions — the same architecture Airwallex uses for multi-currency transfers across 50+ countries.

item.title: API Gateway Explained (ByteByteGo)
item.description: What an API gateway does: authentication, rate limiting, request routing, protocol translation, and service discovery. How it fits into a microservices architecture.

item.title: How a URL Shortener Works — System Design Walkthrough (ByteByteGo)
item.description: End-to-end system design for a URL shortener: hash functions, base62 encoding, database schema, caching strategy, and scaling to millions of URLs.

item.title: Rate Limiter Design — Token Bucket & Leaky Bucket (ByteByteGo)
item.description: Token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, sliding window — the four rate limiting algorithms explained. How to scale rate limiters in a distributed system.

item.title: CAP Theorem Simplified (ByteByteGo)
item.description: Why distributed systems must choose between Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance. Clear explanation with real-world database examples (CP vs AP systems).

item.title: Consistent Hashing Explained (ByteByteGo)
item.description: Visual explainer on consistent hashing — how distributed systems assign keys to nodes and minimize redistribution when nodes are added or removed. Core concept for sharding and distributed caches.

item.title: Message Queues & Event-Driven Architecture — Patterns & Tradeoffs
item.description: Chris Patterson (MassTransit creator) on message brokers vs event streaming, sagas vs routing slips, transactional outbox pattern, dead-letter queues. Transport-agnostic architectural patterns for distributed systems.

item.title: Rate Limiting & High-Traffic Systems — Real Incident Walkthrough
item.description: Mojtaba Sarooghi (Queue-it) on handling flash traffic: 100K to 100M requests in one minute, cold-start failures, DynamoDB at 200K TPS, rate limiting algorithms, and bot detection (98% of traffic is bots during ticket drops).

item.title: Event Sourcing & CQRS — Architecture Deep Dive
item.description: Martin Dilger (author of Understanding Event Sourcing) explains event stores, projections, CQRS, event versioning, and why Kafka is NOT an event store. Practical adoption strategy: 2-day modeling workshop + 1-day build.

item.title: System Design Interviews — The Complete Framework
item.description: Sriram Panyam (ex-Google, ex-LinkedIn) breaks down the system design interview: 5-phase approach, 25 canonical problems, what interviewers look for at each level, and the key mindset shift from buzzword-driven to requirement-driven design. The single best SDI resource.
